pages.title: A obra e a situação

work.title: Little Jack Horner
work.note: Little Jack Horner é uma rima infantil tradicional em inglês, registrada por volta do século XVIII. Ela conta, em poucos versos, a cena de um menino sentado num canto comendo uma torta de Natal. O final é curto e bem-humorado, e a rima torna o texto fácil de lembrar. A referência fala das ameixas de uma torta: these plums, those pies.

pages.title: Ribs in Kansas City · 1/3
paragraphs: My friend Carl and I went to a barbecue restaurant in **Kansas City**. It smelled so good! A man called Aaron said, “**Welcome! Do you want to share?**” “Yes,” we said. “**What’s good here?**”
“**The ribs are great**,” said Aaron. We ordered one rack of ribs. Then he asked, “**Do you want sides?**” “Corn and beans, please,” I said. “**Anything to drink?**” “Two waters, please.”
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: Ribs in Kansas City · 2/3
paragraphs: The food came on one big plate. There was no knife and no fork, only napkins! Carl said, “**Dig in!**” We ate the ribs with our hands. The sauce was sweet and a little smoky. It was “**finger-lickin’ good**”, and we laughed.

I remembered a nursery rhyme from England, “Little Jack Horner”. It is from about the 1700s. A boy sits in a corner and eats a Christmas pie. He pulls out a plum and says, “What a good boy am I!” We sat at a corner table too, and I felt like Jack Horner.

pages.title: Ribs in Kansas City · 3/3
paragraphs: At the end, Carl said, “**I’m stuffed!**” I said, “**Save room** for dessert.” We shared a small piece of pie. It was a perfect lunch, and we will come back soon.
